== History and Origins ==
A theory holds that a family which migrated from {{ill|Bōsō Peninsula|ar|شبه جزيرة بوسو|az|Boso yarımadası|ceb|Bōsō-hantō|cs|Bósó|de|Bōsō-Halbinsel|es|Península de Bōsō|eu|Bōsō penintsula|fa|شبه‌جزیره بوسو|fr|Péninsule de Bōsō|id|Semenanjung Bōsō|it|Penisola di Bōsō|ja|房総半島|jv|Ujung Bōsō|ko|보소반도|nl|Boso (schiereiland)|pl|Bōsō (półwysep)|pt|Península de Bōsō|ru|Босо (полуостров)|simple|Bōsō Peninsula|th|คาบสมุทรโบโซ|tr|Bōsō Yarımadası|uk|Босо (півострів)|vi|Bán đảo Bōsō|zh|房總半島|qid=Q1022115|lt=Bōsō Peninsula}} enshrined its ancestors here<ref name="kamnavi-shinyoshida-sugiyama"/>. Although the founding period is unknown, the ''{{ill|Musashi Shikishiki-ki|ja|武蔵式社記}}'' states, “In Yoshida of Tsuzuki District, there is a small place called Sugiyama where the shrine is located,” while the manuscript compiled during the {{ill|Bunka period|ja|Bunka}}・{{ill|Bunsei|de|Bunsei|es|Bunsei|fa|بونسی (دوره)|fr|Ère Bunsei|ia|Bunsei|ja|文政|ko|분세이|ru|Бунсэй|simple|Bunsei|sr|Бунсеи|sv|Bunsei|tr|Bunsei|zh|文政|qid=Q1327119|lt=Bunsei period}} (1804–1829) – ''{{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|qid=Q11503943}}'' – records details such as “An expanse of two dan and five u, north of the village, with a flight of several stone steps leading up to a torii {{ill|Torii|ar|توري|az|Torii|bcl|Torii|bg|Тории|ca|Torii|cs|Torii|de|Torii|el|Τορίι|eo|Torijo|es|Torii|et|Torii|eu|Torii|fa|توریئی|fi|Torii|fr|Torii|he|טוריאי|hu|Torii|hy|Տորիի|id|Torii|it|Torii|ja|鳥居|jv|Torii|ko|도리이|lt|Torii|ms|Torii|nl|Torii|no|Torii|oc|Torii|pl|Torii|pt|Torii|ru|Тории|simple|Torii|sl|Tori|sq|Torii|sv|Torii|ta|தொரீ|th|โทริอิ|tr|Torii|uk|Торії|uz|Torii|vi|Torii|wuu|鳥居|zh|鳥居|qid=Q234731|lt=Torii}} erected before the shrine: the main hall spans two ken by two and a half ken, and the haiden, facing south, spans three ken by two ken, with the sacred object immovable, belonging to the village’s Shofuku-ji {{ill|Bettō-ji|ja|別当寺|qid=Q11396755}},”<ref name="kanagawa-jinjyacho-sugiyama (shinyoshida)"/> {{sfn|Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki Manuscript, Yoshida Village}}. It is said that the shrine’s sacred treasures and historical records, which were once kept at Shofuku-ji, the temple acting as its Bettō-ji, were completely lost in a fire at that temple<ref name="tsugaruoukoku-sugiyama">[http://www18.ocn.ne.jp/~tugaru/sikinaisyasugiyama.html 武蔵国都筑郡唯一の式内社杉山神社を推理]（津軽古代王国）</ref>.

In {{ill|1908|ab|1908|af|1908|als|1908|am|1908 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1908|ar|1908|ary|1908|arz|1908|ast|1908|av|1908 сон|avk|1908|az|1908|azb|۱۹۰۸ (میلادی)|ba|1908 йыл|ban|1908|bar|1908|bat_smg|1908|bcl|1908|be|1908|be_x_old|1908|bg|1908|bh|1908|bn|১৯০৮|bpy|মারি ১৯০৮|br|1908|bs|1908.|ca|1908|cdo|1908 nièng|ce|1908 шо|ceb|1908|ckb|١٩٠٨|co|1908|crh|1908|cs|1908|csb|1908|cv|1908|cy|1908|da|1908|de|1908|diq|1908|dsb|1908|el|1908|eml|1908|eo|1908|es|1908|et|1908|eu|1908|ext|1908|fa|۱۹۰۸|fi|1908|fiu_vro|1908|fo|1908|fr|1908|frp|1908|frr|1908|fur|1908|fy|1908|ga|1908|gag|1908|gan|1908年|gcr|1908|gd|1908|gl|1908|gn|1908|gv|1908|hak|1908-ngièn|he|1908|hi|१९०८|hif|1908|hr|1908.|hsb|1908|ht|1908 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1908|hy|1908|hyw|1908 թուական|ia|1908|id|1908|ilo|1908|inh|1908 шу|io|1908|is|1908|it|1908|ja|1908年|jbo|1908moi|jv|1908|ka|1908|kaa|1908|kbp|1908|kk|1908 жыл|kn|೧೯೦೮|ko|1908년|krc|1908 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1908|ku|1908|kv|1908-ӧд во|kw|1908|la|1908|lb|1908|lez|1908 йис|li|1908|lij|1908|lmo|1908|lt|1908 m.|lv|1908. gads|mai|१९०८|map_bms|1908|mdf|1908|mg|1908|mhr|1908|mi|1908|min|1908|mk|1908|ml|1908|mn|1908 он|mr|इ.स. १९०८|mrj|1908 и|ms|1908|my|၁၉၀၈|myv|1908 ие|mzn|۱۹۰۸|nah|1908|nap|1908|nds|1908|nds_nl|1908|new|ई सं १९०८|nl|1908|nn|1908|no|1908|nov|1908|nrm|1908|nso|1908|oc|1908|olo|1908|or|୧୯୦୮|os|1908-æм аз|pa|1908|pam|1908|pap|1908|pl|1908|pnb|1908|pt|1908|qu|1908|ro|1908|roa_rup|1908|roa_tara|1908|ru|1908 год|rue|1908|sa|१९०८|sah|1908|sc|1908|scn|1908|sco|1908|sd|1908ع|se|1908|sh|1908.|shn|1908|si|1908|simple|1908|sk|1908|sl|1908|smn|1908|sq|1908|sr|1908|srn|1908|stq|1908|su|1908|sv|1908|sw|1908|szl|1908|ta|1908|te|1908|tg|Соли 1908|th|พ.ศ. 2451|tk|1908|tl|1908|tly|1908|tpi|1908|tr|1908|tt|1908 ел|ty|1908|udm|1908 ар|ug|1908 - يىلى|uk|1908|ur|1908ء|uz|1908|vec|1908|vi|1908|vls|1908|vo|1908|wa|1908|war|1908|wuu|1908年|xmf|1908|yi|1908|za|1908 nienz|zea|1908|zh|1908年|zh_classical|一九〇八年|zh_min_nan|1908 nî|zh_yue|1908年|zu|1908|qid=Q2056|lt=1908}}, the shrine was Ranked among the local shrines in Yoshida Village of Tsuzuki District (which became Nittamura after the 1889 merger)<ref name="kanagawa-jinjyacho-sugiyoshida (shinyoshida)"/>.

== As a Ronsya of Shikinaisha ==
The theory that this shrine is a Shikinaisha existed even before the compilation of the ''Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki Manuscript''. In works such as ''Historical Geography of Musashi Shikinaisha'' (first published in 1966 and revised in 1972 as ''Musashi no Koshā'') by {{ill|Saitō Yoshihiko|ja|斎藤義彦}}, a Shintoist of the Bakumatsu period, and local historian {{ill|Hishinuma Isamu|ja|菱沼勇}}<ref>[http://www6.plala.or.jp/guti/cemetery/PERSON/H/hishinuma_i.html Hishinuma Isamu]（歴史が眠る多磨霊園）</ref>, this view is considered persuasive.<ref>[http://www.okuraken.or.jp/depo/chiikijyouhou/kouhoku_rekishi_bunka/kouhoku52/ History and Culture of Kohoku Ward (Series: Our Town Kohoku, April 2003): No.52 Sugiyama Shrine – a Prominent Candidate]（公益財団法人 大倉精神文化研究所）</ref> Hishinuma Isamu bases his argument on several points: the existence of a minor place name “Sugiyama” in the area {{ill|koaza|ja|小字|ko|고아자|zh|小字|qid=Q5327509|lt=small name}}, the fact that the Mori family – an old family in the region closely connected with the shrine – is said to have a history spanning over a thousand years according to oral tradition {{ill|Q11410744|ja|口伝|qid=Q11410744}}, and the presence of “Asama Tsumuka”, an ancient tomb ({{ill|Kofun|ca|Kofun|cs|Kofun|da|Kofun|de|Kofun|eo|Kofun|es|Kofun|fa|کوفون|fi|Kofun|fr|Kofun|he|קופון (רוגם)|hr|Kofun (grobnica)|id|Kofun|it|Kofun|ja|古墳|ko|고훈|my|ခိုဖွန်း|pl|Kofun (kurhan)|pt|Kofun|ru|Кофун (захоронение)|simple|Kofun|th|โคฟุง|tr|Kofun|uk|Кофун|zh|古墳|qid=Q1141225|lt=ancient tomb}}) on a hill (target: {{ill|Hill|als|Hügel|an|Pueyo|ang|Hyll|ar|تل|arc|ܬܠܐ|ary|كدية|arz|تل|ay|Qullu|az|Təpə|azb|تپه|ban|Bukit|bar|Bichl|bat_smg|Kalnalis|bcl|Bulod|be|Узгорак|be_x_old|Узгорак|bg|Хълм|bh|पहाड़ी|bn|পাহাড়|br|Torgenn|bs|Brdo|ca|Turó|ce|Барз (рельеф)|ceb|Bungtod|ckb|گرد|cs|Kopec|cv|Сăрт|da|Bakke (geologi)|de|Hügel|el|Λόφος|eo|Holmo|es|Colina|et|Küngas|eu|Muino|fa|تپه|fi|Mäki|fj|Dalana|fr|Colline|frr|Huug (berag)|fy|Heuvel|ga|Cnoc|gd|Meall (cnoc)|gl|Outeiro (orografía)|gn|Yvytymi|he|גבעה|hr|Brdo|hu|Domb|hy|Բլուր (աշխարհագրություն)|iba|Bukit|id|Bukit|inh|Гув|io|Kolino|is|Hóll|it|Collina|ja|丘|jv|Punthuk|ka|ბორცვი|kab|Tiɣilt|kcg|Tsok|kk|Төбе|kn|ಬೆಟ್ಟ|ko|언덕|ks|بال|ky|Дөбө|la|Collis|lg|Nabulagala|lld|Col|lmo|Culina|lt|Kalva|ltg|Kaupris|lv|Paugurs|mg|Havoana|min|Bukik|mk|Рид|ml|കുന്ന്|mr|टेकडी|ms|Bukit|mzn|مورروس|ne|पहाड|new|गुँ|nl|Heuvel (landvorm)|nn|Ås|no|Ås|om|Tabba|pa|ਪਹਾੜੀ|pl|Wzgórze|pt|Morro|ro|Deal|roa_rup|Dzeanâ (geografie)|ru|Холм|sa|पारसनाथः|sah|Томтор|sh|Brdo|shi|Tukart|simple|Hill|sl|Grič|sq|Kodra (gjeodezi)|sr|Брдо|su|Pasir|sv|Kulle|sw|Kilima|szl|Berg|ta|குன்று|te|కొండ|th|เนินเขา|tl|Burol|tr|Tepe|tt|Калкулык|uk|Пагорб|uz|Adirlar|vec|Cołina|vi|Đồi|vls|Heuvel|wa|Tiene|war|Mukidbukid|wuu|丘|xmf|გა|yi|בערגל|yo|Òkè|zh|丘|zh_classical|丘|zh_min_nan|Lūn-á|zh_yue|山仔|qid=Q54050|lt=elevated area}}) behind the Mori family that attests to the former power of a local warlord {{ill|dogō|ja|土豪|zh|土豪 (日本)|qid=Q11423883}}.<ref>[http://www.okuraken.or.jp/depo/chiikijyouhou/kouhoku_rekishi_bunka/kouhoku53/ History and Culture of Kohoku Ward (Series: Our Town Kohoku, May 2003): No.53 Sugiyama Shrine in the Ward]（公益財団法人 大倉精神文化研究所）</ref>. In addition, the local ''History of Kohoku Ward'' mentions that the “Mori” in the Mori family is derived from the “guardian forest” ({{ill|Chinju no Mori|id|Chinju no Mori|ja|鎮守の森|simple|Chinju no Mori|qid=Q11651158|lt=Sacred Grove}}) and that the family is locally reverenced as “Sugiyama-sama”. Moreover, nearby in Hayabuchi 3-chōme there exist the [[{{ill|North River Upper Ruins|ja|北川表の上遺跡}}]] and [[{{ill|Kitagawa Shell Mound|ja|北川貝塚|qid=Q11401676}}]], and the ''Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki Manuscript, Yoshida Village'' records that “a large shell mound existed in Yoshida Village of Tsuzuki District” {{sfn|Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki Manuscript, Yoshida Village}}, with the local name “Shell Mound Field” still in use – evidence that archaeological sites in the area have long been known.<ref name="tsugaruoukoku-sugiyama"/> 

Like many other ronsya, the shrine is situated on an elevated spot along the {{ill|Tsurumi River|arz|نهر تسورومى|de|Tsurumi (Fluss)|fa|تسورومیگاوا|ja|鶴見川|my|ဆွတ်ရုမိမြစ်|ru|Цуруми (река)|zh|鶴見川|qid=Q7850292|lt=Tsurumi River}} of the {{ill|Drainage system (geomorphology)|als|Flusssystem|ar|منظومة تصريف|az|Drenaj sistemi|ca|Xarxa de drenatge|da|Flodsystem|de|Flusssystem|es|Red de drenaje|et|Jõgikond|fa|سامانه زهکشی (ژئومورفولوژی)|fi|Uomaverkosto|fr|Réseau de drainage (géomorphologie)|ha|Tsarin ruwa (geomorphology)|hi|अपवाह तन्त्र|id|Sistem sungai|ja|水系|ko|수계|mni|ꯂꯝ-ꯇꯨ|nl|Drainagepatroon|nn|Vassdrag|no|Vassdrag|pap|Sistema di drèinage|pt|Rede de drenagem|th|ระบบลำธาร|tr|Drenaj sistemi|uz|Daryo sistemasi|zh|水系|qid=Q285451|lt=water system}} ({{ill|Hayabuchi River|ja|早渕川|qid=Q11511423}}).
